label: Dispersal account (fan-out)
description: One account paying many in a short window. The dispersal half: once funds have been collected, they are broken up and pushed outward, often to accounts that will each forward again. Detected on the count of distinct recipients within the window.
confounders: Payroll. A small employer paying twenty salaries on the last working day of the month produces a textbook fan-out, every month, forever.
A supplier settling invoices in a batch.
A refund run after a failed service: one merchant, many customers, all within an hour.
notes: Fan-out alone is the weakest of the typologies here, because its innocent explanations are so common and so regular. It is worth much more in combination: fan-in followed by fan-out through the same account within hours is the pass-through shape, and that is a far stronger signal than either half.
